spec: ProgressDesk MS1: the owner-facing definition and planning surface. Complete the existing owner operations to the FUSP/TESP contract: Create Project integrity, definition revision and pending signoff, the planning board and its model-connected formalization, and the owner views of findings, evidence, usage and the signoff policy.

acceptanceConditions: Create Project validates the exact definition chain and both owner signoffs, and refuses a stale displayed draft revision
definition.revise creates a new revision bound to the exact prior revision and refuses a stale expected revision
definition.pending lists the VISP and FUSP revisions that still await an owner signoff
the planning board records topics, meetings, questions and answers as events and rebuilds them from the event log
planning formalization produces structured decisions, a plain-language summary and a draft artifact that keeps every attachment reference
the owner surface exposes pending decisions, milestone findings, acceptance evidence, recorded usage and the milestone signoff policy
the candidate package is imported from the assembled product, not from the factory

features.title: Create Project validates the chain, the signoffs and the displayed draft
features.outcome: The existing Create Project operation validates the exact definition chain and both owner signoffs before it materializes anything, and refuses a stale displayed draft revision instead of creating a different project from the one the owner approved.
features.scope: Only src/progressdesk/desk.py and the route table in src/progressdesk/runtime.py. The operation already exists; this completes it. Do not change the event vocabulary or the planning board.
interfaces: ProgressDeskOperations.chain_digest(definition_refs) -> 'sha256:<64-hex>' over the exact VISP, FUSP and TESP revisions
route verb 'project.create' accepts the optional params definition_refs (dict with VISP, FUSP and TESP) and draft_revision (the digest the owner displayed) and returns the created project id
a missing or stale draft_revision, an unsigned VISP or FUSP revision, or a broken parent chain is refused with a typed error and nothing is materialized
acceptance: Create Project with the exact chain and both signoffs materializes the project
Create Project with a draft_revision that does not match the current chain digest is refused and creates nothing
Create Project with an unsigned VISP or FUSP revision is refused and creates nothing
Create Project with a TESP that does not name the pinned FUSP revision as parent is refused
a retry with the same request id returns the original project and creates no second one

features.title: Owner definition revision and pending signoff
features.outcome: An owner can revise an existing definition revision and can see which VISP/FUSP revisions still await a signoff. The revision is bound to the exact revision the owner displayed: revising from a superseded revision is refused, and the earlier revision's signoff no longer authorises dispatch.
features.scope: Only src/progressdesk/runtime.py (route table and handlers) and src/progressdesk/definitions.py (a read-only pending projection). Do not modify other modules.
interfaces: route verb 'definition.revise' with params definition_id: str, revision: int, content: str -> {'id','kind','revision','contentRef','status':'revised'}
route verb 'definition.pending' with no params -> {'pending': [{'id','kind','revision','contentRef'}]}
Definitions.pending_signoffs() -> list of dicts with keys id, kind, revision, contentRef for VISP and FUSP kinds whose latest recorded revision has no definition.signed-off event
acceptance: definition.revise on an existing definition returns a revision exactly one higher than the supplied revision and records definition.revised
definition.revise with a revision that is not the current one is refused with a typed error naming the stale expected revision
definition.revise of an unknown definition id is refused with a typed error and records nothing
definition.pending lists a VISP revision that was never signed off and omits a revision that was signed off

features.title: Planning board with topics, meetings, questions and answers
features.outcome: The planning surface supports the item model of TESP 5.2 in text: named topics, bounded meetings with a session leader, questions and answers. Every change is an event, the board view is rebuilt from the event log, and participation control stays deterministic rather than the leader's discretion. The existing planning.item.create operation is repaired: it currently fails, so the surface has no working card.
features.scope: Only src/progressdesk/planning.py and the route table in src/progressdesk/runtime.py. Do not change the definition pipeline or the feature list.
interfaces: route verb 'planning.item.create' works again: it accepts summary, optional content, optional provenance and optional topic_refs and returns the created item
PlanningSession.create_topic(name) -> topic dict with topicId and name
PlanningSession.open_meeting(topic_refs, leader, limits) -> meeting dict with meetingId, topicRefs, leader, limits
PlanningSession.record_turn(meeting_id, role, text) -> transcript artifact reference
PlanningSession.ask_question(meeting_id, question) -> question dict with questionId and meetingId
PlanningSession.record_answer(question_id, answer) -> answer dict
PlanningSession.board() -> dict with the existing 'items' plus 'topics', 'meetings' and 'questions' keys
route verbs 'planning.topic.create', 'planning.meeting.open', 'planning.meeting.record', 'planning.question.ask', 'planning.answer.record' and 'planning.board'
acceptance: planning.item.create records a planning.item.created event and returns the item with its itemId
planning.topic.create records a planning.topic.created event and planning.board returns the topic
planning.meeting.open with two topic references records a planning.meeting.opened event naming the leader and the topics
planning.meeting.record stores the turn bytes as an artifact and returns its reference
planning.question.ask and planning.answer.record record their events and planning.board rebuilds both
an unknown meeting id or question id is refused with a typed error and records nothing
rebuilding the board twice from the same event log yields identical output

features.title: Model-connected formalization with structured decisions and preserved attachments
features.outcome: Formalizing planning items runs the configured planning session leader over the items and records what the owner has to check: the structured decisions that were extracted, a plain-language summary, and the VISP or FUSP intermediate draft artifact. Attachment references of every formalized item survive formalization; an image reference is never dropped.
features.scope: Only src/progressdesk/planning.py and the route table in src/progressdesk/runtime.py. The session leader is called through the existing runtime adapter seam; do not add a second transport and do not sign off anything.
interfaces: PlanningSession.__init__ accepts an optional planner callable, invoked as planner(item_payloads) -> dict with keys 'structuredDecisions' (list of dicts) and 'plainSummary' (str)

PlanningSession.formalize(item_ids, definition_id, definition_revision) records planning.item.formalized with payload keys itemId, definitionRef, structuredDecisions, plainSummary, draftArtifactRef, attachmentRefs
the draft artifact is a JSON object with keys documentType, structuredDecisions, plainSummary, attachmentRefs, definitionRef

route verb 'planning.formalize' resolves the planning session leader from config/assignments.json under the role name 'PLANNER' and refuses formalization with a typed error naming the missing planner when no such role is configured
acceptance: a formalized item's attachmentRefs are present in the planning.item.formalized payload and in the draft artifact
the draft artifact contains the structured decisions and the plain summary returned by the planner
the plain summary is non-empty text and the structured decisions are a list of objects
formalization never records a signoff and never authorizes execution
formalizing without a configured planner is refused with a typed error and records nothing

features.title: Owner views of findings, evidence, usage and the signoff policy
features.outcome: The owner can read, in text, what a milestone found, which evidence exists, what the recorded usage was and whether a milestone asks for a human signoff, without editing any internal state file. The existing project.status keeps its shape and gains nothing it should not have.
features.scope: Only src/progressdesk/runtime.py and a new read-only module src/progressdesk/owner_views.py. Read the event log; write nothing except the returned view.
interfaces: route verb 'owner.findings' with params project_id, milestone_id -> {'findings': [...], 'attempts': [...]}
route verb 'owner.evidence' with params project_id, milestone_id -> {'evidenceRefs': [...]}
route verb 'usage.report' with params project_id -> {'usage': [rows with role, executor, provider, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, cost, wallMs, exit, status]}
route verb 'milestone.signoff.policy' with params project_id -> {'milestones': [{'milestoneId','signoffPolicy'}]}
acceptance: owner.findings returns the concrete findings of every failed milestone attempt and the identity of each attempt
owner.evidence returns the acceptance evidence references of the given milestone
usage.report returns one row per recorded usage event and never invents a token or cost value: unknown measurements stay null
milestone.signoff.policy reports the declared signoff policy of every milestone of that project
an unknown project id is refused with a typed error
